messages:
Anya: Follow-up to the transfer RFC. I'm proposing we formalize an explicit midflight "ownership handoff" state model in the edge proxy so it's unambiguous who is liable for requests during retries/rollbacks. Main idea: introduce HANDOFF->REHYDRATE->ACTIVE transitions with a signed HandoffToken (attempt_id + small state blob).

Kai: High level please?

Anya: Simplified: RECEIVED -> STREAMING -> HANDOFF (prepare snapshot + token) -> REHYDRATE (new owner pulls token, rehydrates minimal prefix) -> ACTIVE -> (COMMIT | ABORT). If REHYDRATE fails we emit HANDOFF_FAILED and either revert to original owner or mark ORPHANED for reconciliation.

Ben: Ok but double-execute risk remains. How do we ensure idempotence across owners + retries?

Anya: We attach two stable identifiers: idempotency_key (from client or derived) and handoff_attempt (monotonic). Gateway will reject any execution where handoff_attempt <= last_committed_attempt for that idempotency_key. That covers replay. If upstream can't enforce, we fail fast.

Marta: Observability: please add span events: handoff_prepare, handoff_publish, rehydrate_start, rehydrate_complete, handoff_commit, handoff_abort. Counters: handoff_failures, rehydrate_time_ms, orphaned_time_ms.

ops-bot: incident-bot: note: yesterday's duplicate run recorded in #incidents/3264. This model could reduce that class of incidents.

Kai: Behaviour when client already got partial bytes: do we let client continue receiving from original owner while rehydrate happens, or cut stream and instruct client to resume? Pros/cons?

Anya: Options we debated: 1) transparent resume: stream partials, issue resume token trailer and let client reconnect to new owner; 2) conservative cut: close stream with explicit trailer indicating TRANSFER_REQUIRED so client can replay. My recommendation: support transparent resume only for clients that advertise resume capability (via handshake header) otherwise conservative cut.

Ben: How heavy is the state snapshot? If we snapshot entire KV/prefix it will be expensive and can blow memory.

Anya: Tradeoffs: 1) eager small snapshot (configurable token_count_limit, default 512 tokens) included in the HandoffToken; 2) lazy rehydrate where the new owner requests missing segments on demand from origin using a deterministic rehydrate protocol. We'll start with eager small snapshots to keep protocol simple and measure. If snapshot size > limit we fail handoff with HANDOFF_TOO_LARGE and either keep owner or abort.

Leah: Ops note: make handoff opt-in per-route with rollout controls (percent traffic, clusters). Start at 0.5% internal routes. Add a feature flag to disable snapshoting per cluster.

Anya: Also adding a memory-pressure gate: if node memory usage > X% we short-circuit handoff and prefer abort-to-origin. Documented opt-out annotation required for latency-sensitive routes.

Kai: Can you paste a minimal proto for the HandoffToken so I can check compatibility?

Anya: proto sketch:

```proto
message HandoffToken {
  string token_id = 1;
  string attempt_id = 2;
  bytes prefix_snapshot = 3; // up to N tokens
  map<string,string> meta = 4; // route, flags
}
```

Ben: Billing and rate limits question: which owner is billed during the handoff window? My vote: original owner continues to consume quota until handoff_commit; that keeps user-visible billing stable and avoids double counting.

Marta: agree. Also add metrics: handoff_commit_latency_ms and handoff_orphaned_duration_ms. We should export per-route histograms.

deploy-bot: created INF-2401: "edge: handoff state machine + proto + rollout checklist"

Anya: I'll open the PR with state diagram, invariants, proto and rollout checklist. Will include tests for duplicate suppression and resume semantics.

Kai: Add a small e2e POC: enable handoff on an internal streaming route at 0.5% and collect handoff_success, handoff_failures, duplicates. If rehydrate latency > threshold we revert.

Leah: Don't forget to add an operator kill-switch and an automated watch that flips off handoff if orphaned_rate > 0.1% for 10m.

Anya: Good call. Will add watchdog + alerting.

Ben: One more: implement a deterministic checksum over prefix_snapshot and include it in the token meta so we can quickly validate rehydration integrity and detect corruption.

Marta: +1. Also include the final kbps for snapshot transfer as a metric so we can size the network impact.

Anya: Thanks all. I'll post PR link when ready and ping for quick review. Expected PR by EOD with proto and simple state tests.
